title: feat(claude): Fable resets are offered and redeemed apart from weekly resets
author: juliusmarminge
head: 18e168f6b0b23d3730df7ca5177655ebde03c5f9
body:
Claude now hands out two kinds of banked reset: a **weekly reset** and a **Fable reset**. The Fable reset refills only the Fable allowance and gives back what Fable used on the weekly limit; it does not reset the whole week. T3 Code added every grant into one count and always redeemed whichever grant Claude listed next, so "Use reset" could spend the Fable reset when you wanted the weekly one, and the dialog promised to clear your windows either way.

## Fix

- **Server.** `claudeResetCredits` groups the `cedar_ember` grants by kind, using the same rule as the Claude CLI (2.1.322):
  - a grant that gives back weekly usage is a Fable reset;
  - otherwise its declared `type` decides;
  - otherwise what it clears decides (5-hour, weekly or full).

  Each kind becomes a reset-credit option with its own grant, count, expiry and description.
- **Redeeming.** The instance consume RPC takes an optional `creditId`. The Claude driver redeems that option's grant, after checking it is still offered. As before, one request ID per login is kept until Claude answers, so a retry after an unconfirmed claim resends the same request ID instead of starting a new claim.
- **Clients.** Web (composer, usage page and pool popover) and mobile show one row per kind, each with its own **Use** button. The confirm dialog says what that reset refills. The shared `resetCreditChoices` helper sits in `@t3tools/shared/usageLimits`.

title: fix(desktop): desktop IPC only answers the main app window
author: juliusmarminge
head: 2bb32e0d8e636de018a6c8f4ede5f5ab0427e27a
body:
## Problem

Desktop IPC handlers are registered on the process-wide `ipcMain` and did not check who was calling. Any webContents in the app, including a preview guest showing an arbitrary page, was a valid caller for handlers meant only for the app window, such as the one that returns the local environment bearer token. Only a handful of handlers checked the sender themselves.

## Fix

- `DesktopIpc` now checks the sender centrally. A handler runs only when the call comes from the main window's webContents and its top frame.
  - Async calls from any other sender reject with `DesktopIpcUntrustedSenderError`.
  - Sync calls from any other sender return `undefined` and log a warning, since throwing there would be an uncaught main-process exception.
- The main window is registered before it starts loading, so the preload's startup calls cannot arrive before the guard knows the window.
- New `DesktopIpc.test.ts` covers the main frame (accepted), a subframe of the main window (rejected) and a preview guest (rejected), on both paths.

## Not in this PR

- Preview guests still run with `contextIsolation: false`. Isolating the guest preload is a follow-up.
- The existing per-handler sender checks are now redundant and left in place.

## Verification

- `vp run check:changed` passes.
- Ran the desktop dev build from this branch on Linux. From the real main window, sync and async bridge calls all answered (branding, local environment bootstraps, bearer token, host environment id, client [...]

title: fix(mobile): attaching larger images no longer crashes with a BigInt error
author: juliusmarminge
head: 8963f4c72860997ef724ae6a2b82fe7562ca7926
body:
Attaching images on mobile sometimes crashed with `TypeError: Cannot convert BigInt to number` (in `onProgress` → `onUploadProgress`). It happened only when the native upload sent a progress event, which takes a larger image or a slow connection. Small, fast uploads only get expo's final JS-side event, which uses real numbers.

expo-file-system sends `bytesSent`/`totalBytes` as Swift `Int64`, and in SDK 58 expo-modules-jsi always turns `Int64` into a JS `bigint`, even though expo's types say `number`. `bytesSent / totalBytes` then gave `0n`, and `Math.min(1, progress)` in the upload queue threw.

The fix converts both counts with `Number()` before dividing. That also puts the progress bar right: BigInt division dropped the fraction, so the bar stayed at 0 until the upload finished. The existing upload test now reports BigInt progress from the mocked `file.upload`. Before the fix it fails with `expected [ 0n ] to deeply equal [ 0.25 ]`.

Done by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(server): provider switches hand off started cancelled runs
author: juliusmarminge
head: 507051f7518914371bb30359f0a6754765df75e3
body:
isHandoffSourceRun in apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Orchestrator.ts accepted only completed, failed and interrupted runs. A run that started and then ended 'cancelled' (the provider reported it cancelled; a T3 Stop records 'interrupted') was therefore skipped both on an immediate provider switch (the latestHandoffRun lookup in the send path) and when a queued run on another provider was promoted (the coveredRuns filter). As a result the new provider never saw that run's prompt or response. The predicate now also accepts cancelled runs whose startedAt is non-null. Queued requests cancelled before they started have startedAt null and stay excluded; rolled_back runs stay excluded. The same predicate gates lastDeliveredRunForProviderThread, and there a non-completed run still has to have a provider turn for its attempt, so a cancelled run counts as delivered only if it actually reached the provider. ContextHandoffService's visibleConversationItems already keeps a cancelled run's items, except queued_turn user messages, so the handoff carries the run's visible history with its cancelled status. No new regex or parser. Repro: before the fix the two cancelled rows on factory/repro-34009 failed at assert.isDefined(handoff) and the other five 'hands off' rows passed; all pass after the fix.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#34009

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Do not end the log stream while the output readers are still active.**

`stop()` calls `log.end()` after the `exit` event or after `SIGKILL`. The `readline` interfaces on `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` stay attached. Buffered output can still arrive after `exit`, because the stdio pipes can close later. The `line` handler at Line 136 then calls `log.write()` on an ended stream.

That write emits `ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END`. The `WriteStream` has no `error` listener, so the error can become an uncaught exception. The scenario result is then lost, and `rmSync(home)` in `run.ts` may not run.

Wait for the child's stdio to close before you call `log.end()`. Alternatively, guard the write with `log.writableEnded` and add a no-op `error` listener.

** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Non-interrupt probe failures now silently disable scratch projects, and the diagnostic warning is gone.**

The old code logged a warning that named the base directory and the enclosing repository. The new code does not log.

`Effect.catchCause` turns every non-interrupt failure into `Option.none`. A transient `git` failure, a timeout, or a permission error therefore disables scratch projects. Because of `Duration.infinity`, the result is cached until the process restarts. The user gets only the generic `ScratchUnavailableError` message. No log entry says why.

This also hides the actionable "base dir is inside a Git repository" condition. The retrieved learning says not to swallow git errors, and to surface actionable conditions.

Log a warning before returning `Option.none`. For the repository case, log it in the `Effect.map` step. For the failure case, log it in the `catchCause` handler.

Based on learnings: "don't blanket-swallow errors. Let git errors for actionable, user-fixable conditions ... propagate/surface so the user can act on them."

_Source: Learnings_

title: perf(client): reopening a finished command row no longer refetches its output
author: juliusmarminge
head: f9b5fec67cbfff52aba3e4ee77e648d7bb9e45e9
body:
Reopening a finished command's tool call made the server send its whole output again (up to 64K characters) every time. The command output subscription used `idleTtlMs: 0`, so a collapsed row stopped receiving frames for a running command. That's intended, but it also threw away the final output of finished commands, which never changes. The `turnItem` detail query, used by servers without output streaming and by MCP apps, also dropped finished items after 60 seconds.

- **Subscriptions:** `createEnvironmentSubscriptionAtomFamily` has a new `completedTtlMs` option. When `completeWhen` matches, the final value moves into a small cache atom, and the live subscription is released. Readers get the cached value for `completedTtlMs` after the last one leaves.
- **Command output:** `commandOutput` sets `completeWhen: (view) => !view.running` and caches finished output for 5 minutes. Running commands are unchanged: collapsing the row still ends their subscription immediately.
- **`turnItem`:** the query now routes to one of two families. A settled item's revision is its `updatedAt`, so its answer never goes stale (5-minute idle cache). Live items keep the 60-second cache. Call sites are unchanged.

Web and mobile both read these atoms, so both clients get this.

body: Cause: Orchestrator.appendSteeringMessage stores every steered user_message as completed when it is offered, and the Pi adapter ignored Pi's signals that a steer is queued and later read, so nothing could show that a steer behind a long-running command is still unread. Fix: (1) provider-core gains a `steer.updated` provider event {threadId, runId, messageId, status: pending|completed|cancelled}. (2) The Pi adapter tags steer prompt sends with their messageId. When Pi acks the steer with disposition "queued" it adds the message to the turn's unread list and emits pending. On message_start with role "user" it takes the oldest unread steer and emits completed (Pi reads steers in order). When the turn finalizes, any steer still unread is emitted as cancelled if the turn was interrupted (Stop clears Pi's queue) and completed otherwise. (3) ProviderEventIngestor turns `steer.updated` into a turn-item.updated on the stored user_message (id from idAllocator.derive.userTurnItem), changing only pending/completed items; RunExecutionService routes the event by runId. (4) The web TimelineUserMessageRow marker and the mobile intent badge read 'Steer · waiting to be read' while the item is pending; a cancelled steer shows the existing 'cancelled' status chip. Other providers are unchanged because they never emit the event. title: fix(mobile): tool call commands are highlighted and monospaced like on web
author: juliusmarminge
head: d9354dde25ec0c3c9fe57b14d0513e12182494e3
body:
On mobile, a shell command in an expanded tool call showed as plain, proportional text. Web highlights it, colours scripts embedded in it (heredocs, `python -c`, `node -e`) in their own language, and uses a monospace font.

- **Highlighting:** the mobile work log draws the command through the native highlighter. It uses the same `commandHighlightLanguage` (shell or PowerShell) and `withVisibleControlCharacters` from client-runtime that web uses.
- **Embedded scripts:** `embeddedScripts` (the `unbash` parser) and the `withEmbeddedScripts` overlay moved from web into `@t3tools/client-runtime/work-log/embedded-scripts`, so both clients share them. Web still loads the module lazily. Mobile adds `highlightCommand` on top of its native tokenizer.
- **Monospace on iOS:** `font-mono` was configured only for Android. On iOS it got Tailwind's comma-separated font stack, which native text can't use, so it fell back to the system font. iOS now uses `ui-monospace`, the family the diff and file views already set directly. This fixes every `font-mono` use on iOS, not only this one. Highlighted token runs are plain RN `Text` so they inherit the font instead of resetting it to sans.

title: fix(web): sent messages keep the numbers written on list items
author: tsapa44
head: 92bc9a270109384a8dabd08c7ea217cde62c0163
body:
## Problem

Typing `3. foo` and `5. bar` in the composer shows the items as 3 and 5, and the agent receives them as 3 and 5, but the sent message renders them as 3 and 4. This comes up when answering only some of an agent's numbered questions (for example, the open questions left after a few rounds of a grilling session). The composer draws each item's own marker, while chat markdown follows CommonMark, which numbers an ordered list from its first marker only.

## Change

The sent bubble now shows the list as typed, so the bubble, the composer and the text the agent received agree. User message bodies opt in (`remarkEnableOrderedListNumbers` through `extraRemarkPlugins`); a shared remark plugin then sets `value` on any item whose written number breaks the sequence. It runs before list-indentation recovery, and the recovery step applies the same numbering to blocks it reparses, using their own source.

Agent replies, PR descriptions, plans and file previews are markdown written to be rendered, so they keep CommonMark numbering: a README written as `1.` `1.` `1.` still reads 1, 2, 3. In a user message, `1.` `1.` `1.` stays 1, 1, 1, matching the composer and what the agent received. `ChatMarkdown`'s ordered list gutter sizes for the shown numbers, so a jump like `8.` to `10.` is not clipped.

Nested ordered lists in user messages use decimal markers. Copying rendered lists preserves explicit item values and zero starts. Native mobile rendering is unchanged.

head: 582b3dc152a794140ddc4b34d19fd02860744990
body:
## Problem

ACP Registry command discovery stops after the 128th advertised command. `normalizeAcpRegistryCommands` counts accepted entries and breaks at a hard-coded `MAX_COMMANDS = 128`, so a Devin setup with a large skill catalog silently loses every later skill from the `/` picker. Both the background probe and live `available_commands_update` notifications go through it. On main, 140 advertised skills come back as 128 and the 140th (`poteto-mode`) is missing. `$`-prefixed skills count against the same cap.

## Change

Remove the count cap from `normalizeAcpRegistryCommands` in `packages/provider-acp-registry/src/server/probe.ts`. These stay as they were: the per-entry name, description and hint length bounds, case-insensitive de-duplication, and `$` skill routing. ACP Registry now keeps every valid, distinct advertised command, as the Grok and generic ACP adapters already do. The `ServerProvider.slashCommands`/`skills` contracts have no item limit.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#33757

## Verification

- `vp test run src/provider/AcpRegistryProbe.test.ts` (apps/server): the existing "bounds and de-duplicates advertised commands" case is now "keeps every distinct advertised command and de-duplicates the rest". It advertises 143 entries: `create_plan`, a case-duplicate `CREATE_PLAN`, 140 generated commands and a `$late-skill` at the end. It expects 141 slash commands plus the skill.

title: fix(web): custom snooze footer stays inside the dialog
author: juliusmarminge
head: 84713da0763ddef18ae2f40439322f439a4b8847
body:
## Problem

In the Custom snooze dialog, the footer's "Edit snooze options" button sticks out past the dialog's left border at desktop widths when the interface font is wider than the default (for example a monospace font). The dialog is capped at 24rem, and its three footer buttons (Edit snooze options, Cancel, Snooze) don't wrap or shrink, so `justify-end` pushes the overflow out on the left.

Reproduction on main (`4c361199f4`, web dev server, 1280×800): Settings → Appearance → Interface font = `DejaVu Sans Mono`, then thread actions → Snooze → Custom…. The popup's left edge is at x=448 while "Edit snooze options" starts at x=438. The same thing happens on the Date and time tab and the Duration tab. The default font fits with no room to spare.

## Change

The Custom snooze dialog's width cap at `sm` and up goes from `sm:max-w-sm` (24rem) to `sm:max-w-md` (28rem), the width most dialogs in the app use. The footer now has 400px of content width against the ~370px a monospace footer needs, so it stays on one row with Cancel and Snooze together. The width is rem-based, so this holds across the interface font size setting (12–20px). Below `sm` the dialog is a full-width bottom sheet and is unchanged.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#33740

title: feat(opencode): mirror native goals across clients
author: Yash-Singh1
head: 4b1c14fdc43be45301cb654a439c936d6fc977f0
body:
## Problem

OpenCode 2.2.5 has native `/goal` support, but T3 does not read its goal state. Commands miss the shared native-goal dispatch path, and successful executions can close the T3 run while the goal remains active.

## Change

Advertise native-goal support from the connected OpenCode server, falling back to the probed version before a session connects. Dispatch and turn preparation use that capability, so older versions retain their existing command behavior and provider-switch context.

Read `opencode.goal` through plugin RPC on session load and reconnect, and map `rpc.opencode.goal.changed` into the existing cross-client goal projection. Keep one T3 turn across goal continuation executions. Show, pause, and clear settle locally without waiting for an execution, and delayed control responses cannot settle replacement turns.

Goal reads run outside the event lock and cannot replace newer updates. Unreadable updates invalidate freshness and trigger a bounded refresh; completed executions wait for recovery. Reconnect refresh has one shared timeout, invalidates cached goal freshness, and preserves pending steers. Backfill recovers missed steer-delivery events from persisted native user messages. A native execution still active after reconnect clears the pending completion from its previous execution.

Update the composer guide for OpenCode goal support.

## Scope and approval

Implements https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/33067, requested by the maintainer in [...]

title: fix(server): one finished turn looks up its branch's pull request once
author: juliusmarminge
head: 07c4a7db51730cf7b0ecee64bbda7d100eee4bea
body:
## Problem

When a turn ends, its `checkpoint.captured` events (baselines and the run's own) and the terminal `run.updated` are committed together. `ThreadPullRequestService` queued a separate `refresh: true` lookup for each one. Each refresh skips the branch lookup cache, so one finished turn made two to four GitHub GraphQL `listPullRequestsByHead` calls for the same branch, a second or so apart, spending the user's shared GraphQL budget.

Reproduced on main 4c361199f4: dev server with a fresh database, a project whose `origin` is on github.com, and one Replay turn on a new branch (`t3 thread start --provider devReplay --model todo-list --worktree main --branch …`). After the turn ended, three `ThreadPullRequestServiceV2.synchronize` passes each made a `listPullRequestsByHead` call.

## Change

A thread now has at most one queued pull request lookup. Requests for that thread that arrive while it is still queued join it, and it refreshes if any of them asked for a refresh. The entry is cleared when the lookup starts, so a request that arrives during the lookup queues one more and a change on the host is still read. Full sweeps and backfill are unchanged.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#33744

## Verification

- `ThreadPullRequestServiceV2 reads > looks up a finished turn's branch once for all its turn-end events` (`ThreadPullRequestService.test.ts`). Two threads each commit a turn-end batch (`thread.metadata-updated`, `checkpoint.captured`, `run.updated` comple [...]

title: fix(server): text generation fallback respects project provider settings
author: Muzammil-Bit
head: e343028faada955867e78ca6e222c92cf70727f1
body:
## Problem

When the selected text generation provider can't run (CLI missing, signed out, or usage window exhausted), `TextGeneration.generate` picks another provider. It checks candidates against machine-level provider settings only, so a provider disabled for a project can still write that project's thread titles, branch names, commit messages, PR content and review guides.

## Change

Text generation requests carry an optional `projectId`, and fallback candidates are checked with `resolveProjectProviderInstanceEnabled(settings, projectId, …)` instead of `null`. Thread titles (launch and regenerate), branch names, commit messages, PR content and review guides pass their project. Transcription post-processing has no project, so it stays machine-scoped. The fallback trigger itself is unchanged from #29607.

## Scope and approval

Narrowed from #26979 at the maintainer's request ([comment](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/26979#issuecomment-6751180334)): "Please rebase and narrow this PR to honoring project provider enablement when choosing fallback candidates, which main still checks at machine scope." Replaces #26979, whose branch I can't push to. Related: #26962.

title: fix(server): Claude threads can allow an MCP app for the session
author: t3dotgg
head: 4907789a52e74882c5a803ac259c8e989554347a
body:
## Problem

On Claude threads, ChatGPT Computer Use asks "Allow Computer Use to use X?" on every action, and the card only offered a one-time Approve. A short Computer Use task meant approving dozens of times, often several times for one tool call.

The Computer Use server never remembers an answer. The client must. Codex threads already do this: the card offers "Always allow this session" and Codex answers later prompts itself. The Claude adapter only allowed one-time accepts ([#21903](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/21903)).

## Fix

The Claude elicitation card now offers "Always allow this session". Picking it stores a grant for that MCP server and exact prompt in the adapter session. Later identical prompts get the same acceptance with no card. A different prompt (for example another app) or another server still asks. Grants end with the provider session; "Always allow" across sessions is still not offered.

The Claude CLI strips `_meta` from elicitation replies, so sending `_meta.persist` to the server would do nothing. The grant lives in T3.

Web and mobile need no change; they render the options generically and already show this one on Codex cards.

title: fix(web): prompt suggestions show after a steered turn
author: thelogicmatrix
head: f7a583f9712390c56c75d319fd7a0dbe000a6aba
body:
## Problem

With Suggest next prompt on, a turn that took a steered message never shows its suggestion. Promoting a queued message to Steer cancels that queued run before it starts, and the cancelled run stays the thread's `latestRun`. `usePromptSuggestion` only offers a suggestion for `latestRun`, so the one the provider sent for the run that actually finished is dropped.

## Change

`usePromptSuggestion` now compares the suggestion with the run `announcedRun` picks: `latestRun`, or the last run that ran when `latestRun` was cancelled before it started. That is the same rule screen-reader announcements already use for this case. Thread detail can lag the shell, so the fallback applies only once the runs include that cancelled run. Otherwise cached detail could revive an older turn's suggestion. ChatView passes the thread's runs to the composer for it. The comparison is a small exported function so it can be tested without rendering.

A freshly loaded thread detail never held that cancelled run: the newest history window drops the cancelled queued message, so its run was not selected either. After a reload, or on another client, the suggestion stayed hidden. The newest window now also selects the run the shell reports as `latestRun`, through the same SQL the shell uses (`presentedShellRunId` in `ProjectionStore`). Older-history pages and fork windows are unchanged.

Because the rule is "the latest run never ran", the earlier turn's suggestion also comes back when the queued m [...]

title: fix(server): Commit, push & PR no longer pushes the default branch into itself
author: juliusmarminge
head: 303c3a27bc83b82ee781485e376a9a31e367533c
body:
## Problem

"Commit, push & PR" could push straight to the repository's default branch and then fail to open the PR. Git status decides "default branch" only from the local `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` symref. When that is missing (a repo made with `git init` + `git remote add` + `git push -u`, not cloned) or stale (left at `origin/master` after the remote renamed `master` to `main`), the default branch looks like a feature branch. The client then skips its default-branch confirmation, and the server commits, pushes the default branch into itself, and only then fails at the PR step.

Reproduced on main (331889a135) in the web app, with a GitLab project whose default branch is `develop` and a checkout with no `origin/HEAD`. The button reads "Commit, push & MR". One click moved `develop` from `d67a650` to `7b6ed00` on GitLab, and then MR creation failed. It also reproduces with a local bare remote, for both the missing and the stale `origin/HEAD` cases. A normal clone correctly shows "Commit & push" and the confirmation dialog.

## Change

Before committing, PR actions (`commit_push_pr`, `create_pr`) that are not on a new feature branch now check where the push will go. If the PR would be opened from the base branch into itself in the same repository, and no open PR exists for that branch, the action fails with "`` is the base branch. Check out a feature branch to create a PR." Nothing is committed or pushed.

title: fix(github): a proxy's 403 with Retry-After is no longer reported as a rate limit
author: juliusmarminge
head: 14a9d43f749135b6ffeda52f22b11a61ddbc97a1
body:
## Problem

On a GitHub Enterprise host behind a proxy that requires a TLS client certificate, every PR read failed as "GitHub API rate limit exceeded". The proxy rejects T3's request with its own HTML `403` and `Retry-After: 5`, with no `X-RateLimit-*` headers. `isRateLimited` counted any 403 with `Retry-After` as a rate limit, so `SourceControlRateLimit` paused the host and later reads failed without being sent.

To reproduce on main (8226715813): run the real `GitHubRest` and request-policy layers against a local server that answers HTML `403` with `Retry-After: 5`. The first read fails with `GitHubApiRateLimitError`. The next reads fail in 1 ms with `SourceControlRateLimitPausedError`, and no request is sent.

## Change

A 403 now counts as a rate limit only when GitHub says so: `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, or a body or GraphQL error message that names a rate limit or GitHub's older limit ("You have triggered an abuse detection mechanism"). The GraphQL path hands the classifier its decoded `errors` list without the raw body, so the messages are checked there too. Any other 403 goes through the normal refusal path ("GitHub returned HTTP 403.") and does not pause the host. `Retry-After` still sets the retry time of a real limit. REST and GraphQL share this classifier, so the one change covers both.

This makes the error accurate. It does not make PR reads work through a client-certificate proxy; that needs a transport change and is not part of this PR.

title: fix: hosted agent approval no longer fails with "Your session cannot approve"
author: juliusmarminge
head: ee28af3487cfdf84161ea1d40437448e3273afc9
body:
Testing [#33632](https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/33632) on nightly, Approve on app.t3.codes failed with "Your session cannot approve this request. Enter a pairing code instead."

app.t3.codes only caches a T3 Connect token for environments saved in its catalog (`putRemoteDpopTokenInCatalog`). On the approval page the environment usually isn't saved, so each call minted a fresh credential, two per call in fact. The environment then saw a new session on every call. The approval's CSRF token was bound to the session that loaded the page, so the decision, arriving as another session, was refused. Cookie sessions and plain bearer tokens reuse one session, which is why the server tests passed.

## Fix

- **Server:** for DPoP sessions, the CSRF token is bound to the client's proof key (its thumbprint) instead of the session ID. Every credential the relay mints for that browser carries the same key, and the key can't be used without the browser's non-extractable private key. This also covers a token renewal between load and Approve, which Fable flagged in https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/33632. Cookie and plain bearer sessions stay bound to their session.
- **Client:** the hosted page reuses the call's one authorization instead of authorizing again inside the request. That halves the relay mints and the sessions they leave behind.

title: fix(server): quitting no longer restarts the relay client mid-shutdown
author: juliusmarminge
head: e039e17308b32c280903c5dd4cd82f2457e0d8f0
body:
## Problem

On quit, the desktop app sends SIGTERM to the backend's whole process group. The relay client (cloudflared, spawned `detached: false`) is in that group, so it exits cleanly on its own. The supervisor sees the exit while the desired config is still set, because only the runtime's own finalizer clears it, and that finalizer runs after slower shutdown steps such as stopping an OpenCode server. So it logs "Relay client exited; restarting" and spawns a replacement. The finalizer then has to stop that replacement mid-registration, which adds about 2.3s to the backend stop. A terminal Ctrl+C (SIGINT to the foreground group) does the same.

Reproduced on `main` with the real `CloudManagedEndpointRuntime`, a stub cloudflared in the same process group, and a 1s shutdown step ahead of the runtime's finalizer. Signalling the whole group gave the restart and stops of 3351ms (SIGTERM) and 3353ms (SIGINT). Without the slow step there was no restart and the stop took 91ms.

## Change

The runtime records when the server receives SIGINT or SIGTERM. It uses the same scoped listener pattern `ProviderSessionManager` already uses for group signals, and removes the listeners when the layer closes. Once a signal has arrived, `superviseConnector` still stops the exited connector but returns before restarting it or requesting recovery. Normal crash restarts are unchanged.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#33623

New threads started without an active thread or draft used the first project in sidebar order, even after working in another project. This was visible when creating a draft from Settings or delivering a pending snapshot after reopening the app.

title: fix(desktop): input during window teardown no longer throws in the main process
author: juliusmarminge
head: a364c2af1916ce3795836726553dba9e8333567d
body:
## Problem

Quitting the desktop app with a held ⌘Q (Confirm quit: Hold) can show a main-process `TypeError: Object has been destroyed` dialog. A held quit can fire from the grace timer, so the trailing Q key-up reaches the `before-input-event` listener in `apps/desktop/src/window/DesktopWindow.ts` while the window is being torn down. That listener reads `window.webContents` to call `setIgnoreMenuShortcuts` without an `isDestroyed()` check, and Electron throws on any member access of a destroyed `BrowserWindow`. The sibling `input-event` listener (trackpad scroll begin/end) has the same missing guard.

## Change

Both listeners now return early when `window.isDestroyed()`, the same guard the `zoom-changed` listener and the other handlers in the file already use. In `before-input-event` the guard comes after `quitShortcutHandler(event, input)`, so the quit-hold flow still sees the trailing key-up. The guard is on the window, not `window.webContents.isDestroyed()`, because reading `.webContents` is itself what throws.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#33614

title: ci(mobile): Android PR preview clients build on Blacksmith
author: juliusmarminge
head: 632bc2f22202a117848447d3e24d7b8dd58b5c03
body:
## Why

A PR with the `🚀 Mobile Continuous Deployment` label whose native fingerprint has no client waits about 40 minutes for EAS to build the Android one. The Android store build on Blacksmith (https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/33565) takes about 4 minutes warm.

## What

The Android half of the preview leaves Expo's `continuous-deploy-fingerprint` action, which can only find clients that EAS built. iOS stays on the action and on EAS.

- **`android` job**: computes the fingerprint with the command the action uses, publishes the update to `pr-`, and writes its own comment (fingerprint, install link, update link, QR).
- **`android-build` job**, only when that fingerprint has no client: `eas build --local --profile preview:dev` on `blacksmith-32vcpu` with Gradle, ccache and the pnpm store on a sticky disk, ARM ABIs only. `eas upload` hosts the APK and returns the install page. The build is recorded as a `mobile-android-preview-build/` tag whose message is that link, the same way the store build records its own; the comment is then updated with the link.
- Fingerprints are still what decides. A client is found by its tag first, then among unexpired EAS builds from before this change.
- `eas.json` is untouched, so no fingerprint changes.

## Fork PRs

`mobile-eas-preview-fork.yml` gets the same Android path, since a fork preview only runs when a maintainer applies the label. Two differences, because it runs PR code:

- No sticky disk: the build is cold, so PR code cannot l [...]

threads.body:
🟡 **Medium** `workflows/mobile-eas-preview.yml:251`

With three PRs requesting the same previously unbuilt fingerprint, the middle PR can be left with a “Building on Blacksmith” comment and never receive the install link. `cancel-in-progress: false` preserves the running build, but this concurrency group allows only one pending job, so the third PR cancels the middle PR’s pending `android-build`; use a queue that retains every job or update all affected PR comments when the build completes.

No longer relevant as of f183de5f0102b8147ca8a3297671d733912a16d9

🟠 **High** `workflows/mobile-eas-preview.yml:399`

When a fingerprint-A build finishes after the PR has published fingerprint B, this step passes A's `FINGERPRINT` and client to `mobile-preview-comment.cjs`, which replaces B's client while retaining B's update group; testers are then sent an incompatible client. Reject build-only comment updates whose fingerprint no longer matches the PR's current fingerprint.

🟡 **Medium** `workflows/mobile-eas-preview.yml:221`

An unexpired matching EAS client returned by `eas build:list` is discarded, so the workflow unnecessarily starts a Blacksmith build for that fingerprint. The temporary tag check clears `link` whenever no local build tag exists; remove that override so the EAS fallback link is reused.

No longer relevant as of 0da5c399ea466fcaf4c28660d968aa61d972c28b

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Validate that the parsed state is a plain object.**

`readState` returns any valid JSON value. A marker line such as `` yields an object. The regex only matches `{...}`, so an array or scalar root is unlikely. But the parsed object can still be missing fields or carry non-string fields. `mergeState` then reads `previous.fingerprint` and `previous.client`, and a non-string value flows into `render` and the PATCH body.

Add a check for a plain object with string fields. Return `null` when the check fails. A forged comment that matches the marker is treated as the bot's own comment, so this check matters.

_Source: Learnings_

** Minor** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win**

**Restrict the comment lookup to the token's own comments.**

The lookup selects the first comment on the PR whose body starts with the marker. Any user who can comment on the PR can post a body with that marker. The script then tries to PATCH that comment. GitHub rejects the edit when the token has no permission, so the job fails. The preview comment is never created.

Query `/user` (or compare `comment.user.login` to the token identity) and match only the bot's comments. Note that `/user` does not work with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` for an app installation. Check which token the workflow passes before you choose the identity source.

Also, the `existing === null` loop condition is redundant with the `break`. Keep one of them.

_Source: Learnings_

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Remove the temporary line before merge.**

This line clears `link` whenever the local `refs/tags/$tag` does not exist. The EAS fallback lookup on Lines 217-219 only runs when that tag is missing. Its result is therefore always discarded. Every fingerprint without a tag starts a 32-vCPU build, even when a valid EAS-built client exists. The PR description says the forcing commit is reverted before merge, but it is present in the reviewed revision.

** Minor** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win**

**Set `persist-credentials: false` where the job does not need to push.**

The `android-build` checkout stores the `contents: write` token in `.git/config`. The job then runs PR-branch code with that token on disk: `pnpm install`, Gradle and `eas build --local`. Only the `Record build` step needs the credential. The same applies to the `android` job checkout on Lines 155-159, which holds only a read token. Use `persist-credentials: false` in both checkouts. In `android-build`, pass the token to the push step explicitly.

_Source: Linters/SAST tools_

✅ Addressed in commits 3f28037 to 19e8c6c

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Prevent stale builds from overwriting the preview comment.**

If a build for fingerprint A finishes after the Android job posts fingerprint B, it can replace B’s fingerprint and client link while retaining B’s update link and QR code.

Reject stale build-only updates and coordinate comment writes so an older build cannot overwrite a newer update. Continue accepting build results for the current fingerprint.

🔴 **Critical** `workflows/mobile-eas-preview-fork.yml:89`

Fork-controlled install and build scripts can still read the checkout token from `$RUNNER_TEMP/git-credentials-*.config` after this step, exposing the `pull-requests: write` token even though the Git config check passes. Removing the `includeif` entries does not delete the referenced credential file; capture and delete those files before unsetting the entries in both checkout cleanup steps.

No longer relevant as of 19e8c6c80e7de66a2935e7b20b2367331916173d

** Major** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win**

**Delete the checkout credentials file, not only its `includeIf` entry.**

`actions/checkout@v6` does not write the token into `.git/config`. It writes it to a file under `$RUNNER_TEMP` and links that file with an `includeIf.gitdir:…path` entry. Post-job cleanup deletes the file. This step unsets only the `includeIf` key, so `$RUNNER_TEMP/git-credentials-.config` stays on disk. Later steps run the fork's code: `pnpm install` scripts, app config, plugins and, in `android-build`, Gradle. That code can read the file and get the job `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which has `pull-requests: write` under `pull_request_target`. The removed `persist-credentials: false` setting never wrote this file. The comment on Lines 74-75 says no credentials remain for PR scripts, and this step does not meet that claim. The same defect exists at Lines 243-250.

_Source: Linters/SAST tools_

✅ Addressed in commits 3f28037 to 19e8c6c

** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win**

**Grep only stdout when you extract the install link.**

The EAS CLI documents that `--json` "non-JSON messages will be printed to stderr." `2>&1` merges those messages into `upload.json`. `head -n 1` then takes the first `https://expo.dev/...` URL from either stream. Assume a stderr notice contains an expo.dev URL, such as a project page or a changelog link, and prints before the JSON. The step then records that URL as the install link. The `Record build` step stores it in a permanent tag. Every later run with the same fingerprint reuses the wrong link. `eas-version: latest` lets this output change without notice. The same pattern is at Lines 311-312 of `mobile-eas-preview-fork.yml`.

✅ Addressed in commits 3f28037 to 19e8c6c

🟠 **High** `workflows/mobile-eas-preview.yml:288`

Subsequent Android preview jobs cannot find a successfully uploaded local client through its build record, so they treat the client as missing and cannot reuse it. `android-build` writes tags under `mobile-android-preview-build-test/`, while `android` looks only under `mobile-android-preview-build/`; use the same namespace for both.

✅ Resolved in 632bc2f22202a117848447d3e24d7b8dd58b5c03

🔴 **Critical** `workflows/mobile-eas-preview-fork.yml:229`

Fork-controlled Expo configuration can overwrite `.trusted/.github/scripts/mobile-preview-comment.cjs` before this step runs, so the Comment step executes fork code with `GH_TOKEN` and `pull-requests: write` permission. Checking out the script from `main` first does not keep it trusted once PR code runs; move commenting to a separate job or runner that never executes fork code.

🟠 **High** `scripts/mobile-preview-comment.cjs:113`

A concurrent `android-build` run can replace the newer fingerprint and update group with stale values, so the comment rolls back to an obsolete preview state. The fingerprint guard checks only the earlier read, and this `PATCH` replaces the entire comment body; serialize all comment writers per PR or make the read/merge/write concurrency-safe.

🟠 **High** `workflows/mobile-eas-preview-fork.yml:199`

When the matching Android build tag is already present locally, this step still fetches `origin` after checkout credentials have been removed; that fetch fails for the private repository, so the existing client is ignored and the workflow falls back to EAS or builds another client. Check for the local tag before fetching.

```suggestion
          if git show-ref --quiet "refs/tags/$tag"; then
            link="$(git tag -l --format='%(contents:subject)' "$tag")"
          elif git fetch --quiet origin "refs/tags/$tag:refs/tags/$tag" 2>/dev/null; then
            link="$(git tag -l --format='%(contents:subject)' "$tag")"
          else
            link="$(eas build:list --platform android --build-profile preview:dev --runtime-version "$hash" --status finished --limit 5 --json --non-interactive \
              | sed -n '/^\[/,$p' \
              | jq -r --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '[.[] | select((.expirationDate // "9999") > $now)][0] | select(. != null) | "https://expo.dev/accounts/pingdotgg/projects/t3-code/builds/\(.id)"')"
          fi
```

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Remove the `TEMP-TEST` lines before merge. With them, the build record is never reused.**

The PR description says the test-tag build was removed before merge. Both `TEMP-TEST` lines are still in the reviewed revision, and together they cause two defects:

- Line 249 writes `build=true` on every run. Every run therefore starts a `blacksmith-32vcpu` build, even when the tag lookup or the EAS lookup on Lines 240-247 already found a client.
- Line 288 sets `BUILD_TAG` to `mobile-android-preview-build-test/`. The `android` job looks up `mobile-android-preview-build/` on Line 238. A tag that `Record build` pushes is never found by the client lookup in a later run.

Because of these defects, the 4-minute warm path never applies, and every labeled push pays for a full build. Each run also adds a permanent `-test/` tag to the repository.

Also applies to: 288-288

✅ Addressed in commit 632bc2f

** Minor** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win**

**Push the tag from a separate job. PR code runs earlier in the same job.**

The token stays out of the steps that run PR code. However, before `Record build` runs, the same job runs `pnpm install`, Gradle and `eas build --local` from the PR branch. That code can still change the job state, which persists across steps. For example, it can:

- write `.git/hooks/pre-push`,
- set `core.hooksPath` or `credential.helper` in `.git/config`,
- add a `git` wrapper through `$GITHUB_PATH`.

The `git push` on Line 448 then runs with the `contents: write` token in its argv. A compromised dependency in the lockfile could use this to capture the token. That token can push to any unprotected ref.

To fix this, move the tag creation to a small job with `needs: android-build` and `contents: write`. That job does not check out or run PR code. Pass the link to it as a job output, and create the tag there with `gh api` (`git/tags` then `git/refs`). Reduce `android-build` to `contents: read`.

_Source: Learnings_

title: ci(mobile): dev clients build on Blacksmith, and mobile:install starts that build
author: juliusmarminge
head: 5b58052feba188e748d674c060df7d30b5417217
body:
## Why

A dev client that isn't in the shared cache is built on whichever machine asks first: `gradlew app:assembleDebug` on a small VM (5 to 15 minutes), or an EAS build for iOS where there is no Xcode (10 to 30). Several agents missing on the same fingerprint each build it. The Android store build on Blacksmith (https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/33565) takes about 4 minutes warm.

## What

- **`Mobile Dev Client` workflow.** Builds the emulator and simulator development client for a commit's native fingerprint and uploads it to the native-client cache, under the key `mobile:install` already reads.
  - Android: `blacksmith-32vcpu`, with Gradle home and ccache on their own sticky disk (same recipe as the store build).
  - iOS: `blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-26`, the script's existing Xcode path.
  - Runs on native changes to `main`, and on `workflow_dispatch` (`ref`, `platform`, `abi`, `fingerprint`).
  - On pull requests that change the workflow or the script it builds without the cache and shares nothing, as a check.
- **`mobile:install` starts that build.** On a cache miss it dispatches the workflow for HEAD and waits for the client in the cache, when `gh` may dispatch workflows on `pingdotgg/t3code` and HEAD is on GitHub. A run already building the same client is joined, not duplicated. It builds on the machine instead when it can't dispatch, when the run fails, when HEAD lacks the checkout's native edits (the run fails fast on `--expect-fingerprint`), or with `T3_NATIVE_ [...]

threads.body:
🟠 **High** `workflows/mobile-dev-client.yml:73`

Dispatching multiple clients for the same ABI does not queue every request: while one Android build is running, each new run cancels the previous pending run, and the iOS group has the same behavior. A canceled fingerprint is never cached, so `mobile:install` falls back to a local build and fails on machines without the native toolchain; GitHub replaces pending runs in a concurrency group even when `cancel-in-progress` is `false`. Use a real pending queue or separate groups by client fingerprint.

No longer relevant as of 5b58052feba188e748d674c060df7d30b5417217

🔴 **Critical** `workflows/mobile-dev-client.yml:109`

A pull-request build can write executable Gradle initialization scripts to the same sticky disk later mounted by trusted builds, allowing a PR to steal the cache-write credential and publish a malicious client. This key is shared across PRs, main pushes, and dispatches, and the action commits the disk by default; prevent untrusted PRs from committing to the trusted disk, including by enabling Blacksmith branch protection or using a separate disk.

No longer relevant as of 5b58052feba188e748d674c060df7d30b5417217

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Include the fingerprint in the concurrency group for dispatched runs.**

The group is shared by every `push` and `workflow_dispatch` run for one ABI. It does not include the client's fingerprint. With `cancel-in-progress: false`, GitHub still cancels a previously pending run when a newer run enters the same group. This happens even for a different client.

Example:
1. Developer A dispatches fingerprint X while a build is running.
2. Developer B then dispatches fingerprint Y.
3. Run X is cancelled.
4. `remoteBuildState` reports `failed` for run X.
5. Developer A builds locally for 5–15 minutes.

The comment on Line 72 says runs for one client queue up. The group key does not match that comment. A pending `push` run can also be cancelled by a dispatch for another client.

Add `inputs.fingerprint` to the group key. This keeps one group per client for dispatches. `push` runs keep the shared group.

Also applies to: 185-187

🔴 **Critical** `workflows/mobile-dev-client.yml:94`

Dependency and build scripts can still read and exfiltrate the checkout token: `actions/checkout@v6` stores the Authorization header in a `$RUNNER_TEMP/git-credentials-.config` file, and this step removes only Git config references to it. Delete the referenced credential files before running checkout-controlled code in both the Android and iOS jobs.

No longer relevant as of 5b58052feba188e748d674c060df7d30b5417217

** Minor** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win**

**Remove the checkout token file before dependency scripts run.**

These commands remove Git’s credential references, but `actions/checkout@v6` stores the token itself in a separate file under `$RUNNER_TEMP`. Dependency scripts can still read that file before checkout’s post-job cleanup. Capture and remove the referenced credential file as part of this step. Apply the same fix to the iOS step at Lines 215-216. ([github.com](https://github.com/actions/checkout/blob/v6.0.0/src/git-auth-helper.ts))

Based on learnings, checkout credentials must not remain available to untrusted build steps that do not need repository write access.

_Sources: Learnings, Linters/SAST tools_

✅ Addressed in commit 5b58052

title: perf(opencode): bound usage reads to in-window messages
author: Yash-Singh1
head: 9d67caee5b1aed93642073fb7175a254b5973b91
body:
## Problem

OpenCode usage reads scanned message rows by rowid and loaded full message bodies into JavaScript. Large user messages and old history made cold reads slow and memory intensive, even when only a small time window was needed.

## Change

Use `time_created` to select candidate rowids, then read them in bounded pages within a SQLite transaction. SQLite filters assistant messages and projects only usage fields before returning rows. This keeps scans proportional to the selected window and avoids transferring message bodies that usage parsing does not need.

## Scope and approval

This qualifies for the very small, focused obvious-bug exception in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#prior-approval). The defect is that a 64-row page materializes arbitrarily large message bodies, even though usage needs only a few fields. The resulting server OOM is documented in [#27667](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/27667). The implementation changes only this reader's query strategy and adds regression coverage. It preserves usage totals, schemas, product defaults, and stored history; there is no new feature or workflow.

This also incorporates SQL projection from Julius Marminge's [#27679](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/27679), plus window selection by Tymoteusz Bielski and snapshot handling by maria-rcks from [#26613](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/26613). title: fix(mobile): Android feed stays at its end after the keyboard or sidebar changes
author: juliusmarminge
head: fd7e21188713901e8c575aa8836de876a5007742
body:
Stacked on https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/33599 (`t3code/android-workspace-sequencing`), so one build tests both.

## Problem

On Android, start at the true end of a long thread. Focusing the composer, or toggling the sidebar once, leaves the feed short of the end: the last reply and its timestamp footer stay under the composer, even after the keyboard closes. Opening a thread also landed short. iOS was fine.

## Cause

`ThreadFeed` passed the composer height as a static `contentInset` on Android only (added in https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/5585 to seed the first open). Under Legend List 3.7.2 that prop now works against us twice:

- Legend's core end math (`getContentInsetEnd`) ignores `props.contentInset` off iOS, and RN's Android ScrollView has no `contentInset`.
- `KeyboardAwareLegendList` subtracts the static `contentInset.bottom` from every padding report from `KeyboardChatScrollView` on non-iOS.

So Legend was told the composer padding was `92 − 92 = 0`. The native scroll view still pads by the composer height, which puts the true end one composer height past where Legend thinks it is. Every end target came out short by that amount: initial open, keyboard settle, and the width-change end hold from https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/33459. Instrumented emulator logs before the fix: Legend's end was `2877`, the native end reached by swiping was `2969`, and the reported inset was `0`. After the fix both are `2969`, with an inset of `92`.

head: 5965c6cfbca6a7dd754385bfd3bbf6068641d4d8

## Problem

On wide Android (measured on a Galaxy Z Fold, inner display), the split workspace stutters in ways that aren't CPU-bound. They come from the order things happen in:

- **Sidebar open:** the detail pane stays full width during the slide, clipped at the right edge. It only rewraps after the slide stops, about 75 ms later, in one visible frame.
- **Composer focus:** the composer moves first. The pane then goes wide, and the header only goes compact about 166 ms later in a second whole-tree render, while the sidebar is already leaving.
- **Composer blur:** like sidebar open, the pane stays wide and clipped until the keyboard is fully gone, then rewraps at rest.
- **Keyboard while scrolled into history:** every keyboard open and close re-wrapped every message twice, because the sidebar left for the keyboard and the pane went from 581 to 921 dp wide and back. The feed reflowed and landed somewhere different each time, and after closing the native scroll position sometimes kept drifting while the rows settled.

title: fix(server): a queued message that names no model keeps the model picked ahead of it
author: juliusmarminge
head: 6136b5f462c716400f5994d8d8805f28d4e4cbb8
body:
## Problem

A model picked on a queued message only reaches the thread when that message's run starts. A message that names no model and is queued behind it (an MCP `t3_thread_send`, a server or agent message, a scheduled wake) captured the thread's old model. When the queue drained, it switched the whole thread back to that model after the picked run, with avoidable cache misses. Reproduction: a thread on model A runs `/compact`. The user picks model B and sends with Steer, which falls back to the queue because compaction cannot be steered. Another thread then calls `t3_thread_send`. title: fix(server): quitting stops an agent-device daemon left by an earlier server
author: juliusmarminge
head: e0f5828925a1fe082820bb089e23af2636c95385
body:
## Problem

The local agent-device daemon runs with its idle timeout disabled, because the server is supposed to stop it on shutdown. On main, the server only stops it when that same server process started or reused it during the session. A daemon left by an earlier server (for example one the desktop SIGKILLed after its 5 s quit grace, or one that crashed) is never stopped by any later graceful quit, so it keeps running under the app's executable indefinitely.

Reproduction on main (Linux, real server): put a live agent-device 0.21.31 daemon in the worktree's T3 state dir, start the server with that base dir without touching devices, then SIGTERM it. The server exits in 980 ms and the daemon is still running.

## Change

- `stop` (the shutdown finalizer, also used when device support is turned off) and `stopAgent` (turning agent device access off) now stop whatever daemon `/device/agent-device/daemon.json` records, whether or not this process started it. The process-local `agentToolRef` is gone.
- When no `daemon.json` exists, nothing is spawned, so a normal quit costs nothing extra. When `daemon.json` records a pid that is no longer alive, the stale record is removed and nothing is spawned either. Otherwise the stop uses agent-device's own `daemon stop --state-dir` on T3's own state dir, which checks the process identity before signalling it.
- The CLI comes from the agent-device version the daemon recorded when that install is still on disk, falling back to the current pin [...]

title: fix(web): pane slides no longer crash below 100% zoom
author: flamboh
head: 2b2e1d8ab15dabdf07f1cc80d979cef574ddc8d4
body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 on behalf of Oliver**

Fix for the redesign stack, targets layer 6 (#28845).

## Problem

Below 100% browser zoom on a non-Retina screen (device pixel ratio under 1), a pane that gets retargeted mid-slide by less than a device pixel crashes the pane layout effect with `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'entry' before initialization`. It can also happen at 1x when the leftover move is exactly -0.5px.

`slide()` skips moves under 0.5 CSS px, but `playMotion` rounds keyframes to whole device pixels. At 0.75x a 0.6px move rounds to 0px on every keyframe, so `playMotion` finishes at once and calls `onFinish` while `slide()` is still building `entry`.

## Fix

`slide()` now skips a move when it rounds to 0 device pixels on both axes, using the same `toDevicePixel` rounding as the keyframes. A move it lets through always has a first keyframe that differs from the last, so `playMotion` never finishes synchronously from `slide()`. Moves that show no change still rest right away and run their `onRest`, as before.

## Validation

- New browser test `apps/web/src/motion/paneSlide.browser.test.tsx`: at `devicePixelRatio = 0.75` it starts a slide, pins the animation where the pane shows ~0.57px off a whole pixel, then retargets to that whole pixel. It throws the `ReferenceError` on the layer tip and passes with the fix.

## Problem

Some steers interrupt the running turn and restart it with the steer as the new input. title: perf(shared): speed up escaped Markdown in long PR descriptions
author: AksharP5
head: 6aa0bb29dd73878b7bed58f568069b0c244889c1
body:
## Problem

Opening a mobile PR description with many escaped identifiers repeatedly scans the whole paragraph to decide whether each escape belongs to a Windows path. A 38,960-byte description with 2,000 metric names triggers 68.6 million characters of drive-path regex input.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#33436

## Change

Check only the final non-whitespace word before each escape. The existing expression cannot match a path across whitespace, so the preceding words cannot change its result. The path expression, preserved backslashes, link destinations, and parsed output stay the same.

Finding that word must not rescan text either: a first version walked back one character per escape, which made long whitespace-free runs (comma-joined identifiers, CJK prose) about 10× slower than main. Text nodes only grow by appending while mdast-util-from-markdown builds them, so each text node now remembers how far it has been scanned and where its current word starts, and a native `/\s/g` search covers only the newly appended text.

## Scope and approval

One focused shared-parser performance defect, reproduced through the existing mobile PR-description/image-gallery path. The correction is confined to the escape handler and its regression tests, with no product behavior, defaults, contracts, or settings changes. Submitted under the small, obvious-bug exception in CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: perf(server): opening a long thread reads from its latest segments, not its whole history
author: t3dotgg
head: b0d78c7dfb6942186a11e9fa0fadd214c88afb96
body:
Opening a thread on a long history was slow because the snapshot window cost grew with the whole thread, not with the window. On zbook, a thread with 73,568 items at the time (347 MB; 73,967 when counted later) took 7.6 s in this query. It also holds the single SQLite reader, so other reads wait behind it.

## Cause

Every client subscribes with `deferWork`. That path groups completed work into "N more items" rows with `work_segments` (a window function, per-item joins, and a payload `LIKE`). It ran over every item since the user-turn boundary. With fewer than 12 user turns (long agent runs, steers, wakes) that boundary is 0, so it walked the full thread. With more turns the boundary can still sit far back.

Real fleet counts, measured read-only:

- zbook slow thread: 73,967 items, 7,883 never-foldable (about 10%), 14 turn starts. The old start covered effectively the whole thread. The newest 502 never-foldable rows span 3,679 items.

title: perf(server): MCP tool calls no longer read the caller's whole thread
author: t3dotgg
head: 6cb3e96d219a8927586ddd629d36996d9222a27d
body:
Every thread-scoped MCP call (`delegate_task`, `task_status`, `t3_thread_*`, `request_secret`, `create_threads`, `orchestrator_capabilities`, ...) loaded the caller thread's runs, user messages, provider threads and turns, runtime requests and context transfers. On zbook, one call from a thread with 73,568 turn items spent 8.6 s in `loadThreadCaller`, inside one reader transaction. The server has one SQLite reader, so the sidebar's `getThreadShell` waited 6.6 s behind it and a thread open took 7.8 s. The first acknowledgement of a delegated result also read every parent run, node, attempt and subagent (5 s on the fleet trace).

## Fix

- Callers read only the caller's thread row, plus its active runs where the active run is used (cross-thread writes, scheduled tasks, `delegate_task`, `request_secret`, `create_threads`). `t3_thread_list`, `t3_thread_read`, `t3_thread_wait` and `orchestrator_capabilities` read only the thread row. The `parent` type is `Pick`, so a caller that needs another field fails to typecheck.
- A status-only run filter now emits `ORDER BY +ordinal`. Before, SQLite walked every run in the `(thread_id, ordinal)` index to skip a sort. Now a status index reads only matching runs.
- A read by id (`runIds`, `nodeIds`, `subagentIds`, `messageIds`) now uses the primary key. Before, SQLite walked every row of the thread in its thread index to find the ids. On a real thread with 34,195 nodes, one node read took 307,792 SQLite VM steps. It now takes 42. This applies [...]

title: fix(server): opening the branch menu no longer wipes PR status
author: juliusmarminge
head: 456327574c52ad1c7624083bb97eaf382edd1732
body:
## Problem

Opening the branch menu sends `vcs.refreshStatus` with `localOnly: true`. When no remote status was cached, or the branch had changed, that refresh cached an empty remote entry (`{ value: null }`) and published `remoteUpdated: null`. Every reader takes that entry as "the remote was read and has no PR":

- **Overlap:** if the subscription's first remote read is still running, the refresh overwrites the PR, upstream and ahead/behind counts that read just cached. They stay empty until the next poll, or until a full refresh when automatic fetch is set to 0.
- **Before any remote read:** the turn-end `refreshPullRequestStatus` returns without reading, because it skips when `cached.remote?.value === null`.
- **After a branch switch:** the turn-end PR refresh skips in the same way. A subscription that opens afterwards finds a cached remote and waits a full interval before its first read.

## Change

The local-only path of `VcsStatusBroadcaster.refreshStatus` now refreshes local status only and returns the cached parts. It no longer writes a remote entry, invalidates the remote cache, or takes the remote write lock.

- **Branch switch:** `updateCachedLocalStatus` already drops the old branch's remote and publishes `remoteUpdated: null`.
- **Invalidation:** `readRemoteStatus` already invalidates the remote cache before every read.

The only caller (the branch menu) ignores the RPC result and gets status from the stream.

title: fix(web): panel resize handles follow touch drags
author: juliusmarminge
head: c8c3e16a66ed2dd8d61b464c36980a4a548507a1
body:
## Problem

On a touch screen (Chrome on an Android tablet or Googlebook), dragging the resize handles between panels does not follow the finger. The terminal drawer, the right panel, the file explorer column and the sidebar rail move about 20px and then stop. The browser takes the gesture over as a pan and sends `pointercancel`, which ends the drag. The handles are also only 6–8px wide, so a finger that lands slightly off one misses it entirely.

Reproduced on main `23e3465` in Chromium with real touch input (CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`, 1280×800, `(pointer: coarse)`). Opening the bottom and right panels and dragging each handle 80px moved it 20px and ended in `pointercancel`. The same drags with a mouse moved 80px.

## Change

- Every panel resize handle gets `touch-action: none` (`touch-none`), so the browser never claims the touch as a pan and the drag stays with the finger until release. This covers the shared `RightPanelResizeHandle` (right panel and file explorer), the terminal drawer handle and the sidebar rail. Taps on the rail behave as on main (`touch-action` does not suppress clicks).
- On any touch-capable device (`any-pointer-coarse:`, so a laptop with a touch screen and a trackpad counts too), the drawer and right-panel handles widen to 16px. The drawer handle grows downward, because the drawer clips above its top edge.
- With several terminals open, only the terminal sidebar's split/new/close buttons sit above the taller drawer handle, so they keep their ta [...]

([w3.org](https://www.w3.org/TR/mediaqueries-4/))

title: fix(mobile): medium Android windows keep the rail's room and the sidebar's place
author: dongxingong

body:
## Problem

On a 600-720dp Android window the sidebar floats over a page. Two things go wrong in that mode:

- `floatingSidebarAnimatedStyle` (`left: renderedRailWidth`) is only in the style array while the sidebar floats. When the list comes back and the sidebar docks, the style is dropped, and Reanimated keeps the last value of keys a dropped animated style set. title: perf(server): user-only message reads use the user-message index for ordinals
author: juliusmarminge
head: e59d3df56944267faea8e261b9468438c48823d3
body:
Cross-machine `waitForThread` re-reads a thread's user messages on every evaluation. To order them, `ProjectionStore` looks up each message's first turn-item ordinal with `type IN ('user_message', 'assistant_message')`. That predicate can't use the partial `orchestration_v2_projection_turn_items_user_message_idx`, so SQLite walks every turn item of the thread through `thread_run_idx` and reads each payload.

Fleet traces (24h ending 2026-11-08 09:00) show it as the top slow personal sqlite statement: 103 executions over 150 ms on nucbox-1 (max 320 ms, 16.5 s total), up from 38 the day before. They come from `OrchestratorMcpService.waitForThread` → `ThreadManagementService.waitForThread` → `orchestrationV2.threadManagement.evaluate` → `OrchestratorV2.getThreadRecords` (`messageRoles: ["user"]`). `settleAfterRun` uses the same filter.

**Fix:** when every loaded message is a user message, query `type = 'user_message'`. The literal equality matches the partial index's `WHERE`. Mixed or assistant reads keep the old predicate. The rows are the same: on a real 14 GB database, all 8,053 user-role messages map only to `user_message` turn items.

USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY
```

USE TEMP B-TRE [...]

title: fix(server): repos without a remote no longer record failed spans on status refresh
author: ferhtgoldaraz
head: f7e6f98b2f69f9b7691244ff1a6aea8ce1c59bef
body:
## Problem

In a git repo with no remote, every status refresh records a failed `resolvePrimaryRemoteName` span, and Settings → Diagnostics counts each one as a failure. Behavior is fine: the status and base-branch callers catch "No git remote is configured" and fall back to local branches. Only the span is wrong. Repro steps are in pingdotgg/t3code#32904.

## Change

In `GitVcsDriverCore.ts` the lookup now answers `null` when there is no remote, so its span (same name, `resolvePrimaryRemoteName`) succeeds. The public `resolvePrimaryRemoteName` wraps it without a span of its own. It turns `null` into the same `GitCommandError` with the same operation and message, so the driver interface and every caller stay unchanged:

- Status and base-branch callers keep recovering, as before, but no failed span is left behind.
- Callers that need a remote (`fetchRefCommit`, `fetchRefIntoBranch`, PR checkout) still fail with the same error, in their own span.
- Push keeps its own error ("Cannot push because no git remote is configured…") from `resolvePushRemoteName`. That function falls back to this lookup, so a no-remote push also stops leaving a failed child lookup span; the push span itself still fails.

Same idea as pingdotgg/t3code#29070: an expected answer is not a failed span, and real git errors (for example from `git remote`) still fail the span.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#32904

title: fix(server): a restart that misses its turn starts as a new turn
author: juliusmarminge
head: 3e9ad883503f8d3fb8d729677a41a1ab5424c074
body:
## Problem

`t3_thread_send` with `mode: "restart"` resolves its target run before it dispatches `message.dispatch` (`restart_active` with a `targetRunId`). If that run completes, is interrupted, or is reached by a Stop or `t3_thread_interrupt` before the orchestrator handles the command, the restart fails with `orchestration_error` "Target run … is stopping|completed|interrupted and cannot be steered." or "No running provider turn found for active run …", and the message is lost. Client restarts (`deliveryIntent: "restart"`) take the same path. A `steer` in the same position already starts as a new turn.

## Change

In `message.dispatch`, a `restart_active` becomes `start_immediately`, like the existing late-steer fallback, when its target:

- is no longer active,
- is still running or waiting but its provider turn has already ended (completed, interrupted, failed or cancelled; the run settles in a later event), or
- has been reached by Stop.

A restart means "interrupt the turn, then start this message"; once the interrupt has happened, only the start is left. `start_immediately` already queues behind a run that is still settling and follows the usual queue rules: a client send releases a queue Stop held, and an agent or server send waits behind it, as plain sends do. An explicit steer into a stopping run is still refused, unless its turn already completed (the existing late-steer fallback).

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#32891

Triaged via the automated iss [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Deliver an MCP restart after Stop when the queue is held.**

If Stop holds an existing queued run, an MCP restart dispatched while the target is still active inherits that hold. The restart can then remain undelivered until a manual resume. If no queued run is held, it does not inherit a hold.

Make the restart deliverable without releasing the runs that Stop already held, or return `thread_not_sendable` so the caller can retry. Add a test with an existing queued run, `thread.stop`, and an MCP restart.

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Fix the TypeScript error: `status` can be `"failed"`, but `turn.terminal` rejects it.**

The CI typecheck fails with TS2322 at this location. The matrix includes `status: "failed"`. The `turn.terminal` event type accepts only `"cancelled" | "completed" | "interrupted"`. This blocks the build.

Map `failed` to a valid terminal status for the event. Alternatively, build the event with a `failure` payload if the type has a failed variant. Check the `turn.terminal` event definition for the correct shape.

   

_Source: Pipeline failures_

title: fix(server): removing a queued completion message keeps its siblings' wakes
author: juliusmarminge
head: 01c23e8ec6ebcd54120d13998b88c4d5da16a64d
body:
## Problem

When an agent cancels one queued delegated-task completion message (`t3_queue` with `action: "cancel"`, or Remove on the queued message), the server disposed the whole completion cohort of the run that spawned the task. Sibling tasks from that run that were still running were marked `disposed` too. When they finished, their results were saved but never woke the parent.

Reproduction: a parent run starts async tasks A and B. A finishes while the parent is busy, so A's completion wake is queued. Cancel that queued wake, then let B finish. B's result is saved with `completionDelivery: disposed`, and the parent is never woken.

## Change

- `dispatchQueuedRunCancel` now disposes only the tasks the cancelled message carries. It passes the message's `taskIds` to `disposeDelegatedCompletionCohort` as `interruptedWakeTaskIds`, which the interrupt path already uses for the same case.
- The cancel then cancels the requested run itself, using the existing `emitQueuedRunCancellation`. This replaces a copy of those events that was written out inline.
- When the cancelled run ends, `finalizeDelegatedCompletionDelivery` clears the delivery, or reserves a new one for a sibling that finished in the meantime. A sibling that finishes later gets a new wake.
- `thread.settle` also cancels queued wakes through this function, and it keeps disposing the whole cohort (`disposes: "cohort"`). A sibling that finishes after the user settled the thread still cannot wake it and unsettle it.
- S [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Keep the cohort open after wake-scoped cancellation.**

If a queued wake carries every current task, cancellation disposes the cohort. The active parent can then spawn another async task, but its completion is disposed instead of waking the thread.

Keep an open cohort open for wake-scoped cancellation even when no sibling exists yet. Preserve whole-cohort disposal for settlement and Stop.

## Problem

The dev database seed (`vp run migrate-dev-db`, and the first `vp run dev` in a worktree) copied kept threads' projection payloads verbatim. That copy included each pull request link's active `watch`. On a stopped, unsettled thread the dev server's `PullRequestWatchReactor` then swept that watch at startup and read the pull request from the host with this machine's credentials. `pruneSnapshot` in `apps/server/scripts/migrate-dev-db.ts` now rebuilds `$.pullRequests` without `$.watch` on every kept thread whose links carry a watch, in the same transaction that clears the rest of the pending work. The links themselves (URL, snapshot, stack, `endedWatch`) stay, so the UI still shows the thread's pull requests.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#32736

## Problem

Two SSH launches against the same remote T3 home at the same moment (two desktops reconnecting to one host after its server stops, or two aliases for one host) both pass the "is a server running" check, pick the same port and start `t3 serve`. `REMOTE_LAUNCH_SCRIPT` in `packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts` holds one lock per remote T3 home (`~/.t3/ssh-launch/.launch.lock`), using the same noclobber PID-file idiom as the runner's install lock. A launch takes it after the runner is resolved (a cold archive download stays outside it) and keeps it through the runner comparison, reading the records, the start and the readiness wait. A waiting launch then finds the first server:

title: fix(pi): Pi models whose provider ID contains a slash can be selected
author: juliusmarminge
head: bf2902176ccbe799639e46f3834935a0e5328f22
body:
## Problem

When a Pi provider ID contains `/`, Pi turns fail to start with `Pi RPC set_model failed: Model not found: `. The pi-llama-cpp extension names its providers like this by default (`llama-server=http://192.168.0.2:8080`). T3 shows each Pi model as the slug `${provider}/${id}`, and the adapter split that slug at the first `/` before calling `set_model`. For such a provider, the split sends `provider: "llama-server=http:"` and Pi finds no model. The picker lists the model, but it cannot be used.

Reproduced on main with real Pi and an extension that registers a provider `hub=/v1`. The model shows in the picker, and sending a message fails with "The provider could not start this turn". The server log shows `PiRpcError: Pi RPC set_model failed: Model not found: hub=/v1/`. A Pi model whose provider has no `/` replies normally in the same thread.

## Change

`parsePiModelSlug` becomes `resolvePiModelSlug(slug, reportedModels)`. It returns the `{provider, id}` pair that Pi's `get_available_models` reported for that exact slug, and falls back to the old first-`/` split only for slugs Pi did not report, such as custom models. Splitting at the last `/` would break model IDs that contain `/` (`openrouter` / `openrouter/auto`), so the lookup uses Pi's reported pairs. When two reported pairs join to the same slug, the first one wins, the same pair the model picker shows.

- **Adapter:** it already requests `get_available_models` once per session to learn context windows. It now  [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Refresh the model inventory after it changes.**

When Pi reloads extensions or replaces a session, its available models can change. This guard keeps the first successful inventory for the entire adapter session. If a later inventory adds a provider whose ID contains `/`, `applySelection` cannot find it and sends `set_model` the first-slash fallback instead. Pi then rejects a model that a refreshed picker can show. Refresh the cache after a session replacement, or retry discovery on a cache miss before splitting the slug. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/earendil-works/pi/v1.4.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md))

✅ Addressed in commit 0e41937

** Minor** · **Performance & Scalability** · **Quick win**

**Avoid blocking on discovery for unambiguous cache misses.**

A newly registered `provider/model` can be available in Pi but absent from the session cache. The refresh can delay `set_model` by up to 15 seconds even when the first-slash split identifies the same pair. Preserve reported pairs when avoiding this wait.

title: fix(opencode): show questions asked while OpenCode wakes a session on its own
author: juliusmarminge
head: d51f3541e31d2ad30e9bf8a7b55b75d4597fd40c
body:
## Problem

When OpenCode 2 wakes an idle session on its own (for example, when a background subagent reports back) and the model calls `question` before T3's continuation run starts, the question is never shown. The form stays open in OpenCode, the run stays "running", and later reports and user messages queue behind it until someone cancels the form outside T3.

`form.created` carries its session only at `data.form.sessionID`; every other session event, including `permission.asked`, has `data.sessionID`. `sessionOfEvent` read only `data.sessionID`, so the form was never held with the wake's events. `sessionOfEvent` reads `data.form.sessionID` for `form.created`. The form is now held while the wake runs and replayed into the continuation turn, exactly like a `permission.asked` in the same position.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#32430
