title: fix(server): blank .gitignore lines no longer make checkpoints drop new files
author: juliusmarminge
head: 049b1e8e9cdb888d0090c1f5240f9ae027f8b68e
body:
## Problem

Checkpoint capture decided whether the workspace is an ignored project directory with `git check-ignore --no-index .`. Git's ignore parser turns a blank CRLF line (or a spaces-only line) in any ignore source into an empty pattern, and that empty pattern matches `.` because Git normalizes it to `""` at the root or `sub/` below it. A normal workspace was then treated as ignored:

- at the repository root, capture staged with `git add -u`, so untracked files were left out of the checkpoint, and restoring that checkpoint (`git restore` + `git clean -fd`) deleted them;
- in a subdirectory with no tracked files, capture failed with "The workspace directory is ignored by its Git repository".

Reproduced on Linux with Git 2.43 (the reporter used Git for Windows 2.56 with `core.autocrlf=true`, which writes such CRLF lines on checkout):

```
$ printf 'a.txt\r\n\r\nb.txt\r\n' > .gitignore
$ git check-ignore -v --no-index .
.gitignore:2:	.
$ git ls-files --others --exclude-standard
.gitignore
new.txt
```

## Change

`resolveCaptureRepository` adds `--show-prefix` to the `rev-parse` it already runs (its old-Git fallback reads the prefix separately). At the working-tree root the probe is skipped, since the root can never be an ignored directory. Below it, the probe asks about `../`, which Git resolves to the slash-less repo-relative path: an empty pattern cannot match it, while rules that ignore the directory itself (`sub/`, `sub`, an ignored parent) still do, so the ignored-pr [...]

title: fix(server): linked projects keep their repository identity while it refreshes
author: juliusmarminge
head: 893e2e43efd233ee7cdf6e134fb191ec069f429f
body:
## Problem

With linked environments, a project's `repositoryIdentity` in a T3 server's shell snapshot turns `null` once a minute even though its git remote never changed. `ProjectEnrichmentService.peek` reads `Cache.getSuccess`, which returns nothing for an expired or still-refreshing entry, and the success TTL is one minute. A client with no identity on record for that copy groups it by path, so it splits out of its repository group. `ProjectService` readers (e.g. remote delegation project matching) see the same `null`.

Reproduced on a real server built from main: one project whose origin is `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, with `GET /api/orchestration/shell` polled every 10 s. The identity read `null` at 06:15:58 and 06:16:58, one minute apart, with no change to the repo.

## Change

`ProjectEnrichmentService` remembers the last successfully resolved identity per workspace root. The map is capped at the cache capacity and drops the oldest entry first. `peek`/`getAvailable` fall back to it when the cache has no fresh success: the entry expired, its refresh is pending, or the refresh failed. The fallback keeps `repositoryIdentityResolved: false`, so `resolvedRepositoryIdentityRoots` still lists only freshly resolved roots.

- A new successful resolution replaces the remembered value, and a resolved `null` (remote removed) clears it.
- `invalidate` clears it, along with the root's in-flight lookup token, so a lookup that started before `invalidate` cannot overwrite a n [...]

body:
## Problem

`preview_evaluate` rejected top-level `await` with `SyntaxError: await is only valid in async functions and the top level bodies of modules`, so `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 100)); location.pathname` failed although a devtools console accepts it. Only when the page's own parser rejected it, and the expression contains `await`, does it send the same call once more with `replMode: true`, the devtools console's mode. A parse rejection is a `SyntaxError` with a `scriptId` and no stack, so nothing ran. This rules out the other `SyntaxError` cases:

- Once the 15 s limit has fired and terminated the evaluation, a late classic response never triggers the retry.

Fix for the redesign stack, targets layer 6 (#28845).

## Problem

In a chat with its side pane open (a diff or pull request on the right), dragging a thread from the sidebar onto the chat's right half shows "Side by side" over that half. The drop then puts the new chat at the far right, past the side pane. You'd expect it between the two, where the preview was.

A drag-and-drop "Side by side" now lands exactly beside the pane you dropped on, on the side the preview shows. This covers sidebar threads and tab drags, which share the same drop path. Commands keep the old rule: Ctrl+D, agent-opened surfaces, and "Open to the side" in the sidebar menu still put the new chat after the side pane, since nothing previews where they go.

`layoutModel.test.ts` checks that new and moved chats land between a chat and its side pane for exact splits, while commands keep companion grouping. The regression fails on the current layer 6 base.

## Before / after

What to look for: before, the chat dropped on the left pane's right half ends up past the Diff pane on the far right; after, it lands between the chat and the Diff pane, where the "Side by side" preview was.

title: fix(web): sidebar rows no longer slide through each other
author: flamboh
head: 64d089c6174cdaed62cbc154931db3fd36b863b3
body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 on behalf of Oliver**

Fix for the redesign stack, targets layer 1 (#28839).

## Problem

Sidebar rows slide through each other, so you see one title printed over another. It happens when you settle, snooze or pin a thread, when a turn starts or ends, when you collapse a folder, and when you switch the project filter. The redesign's see-through row surfaces make it easy to read both titles at once. `Sidebar.motion.ts` is the same on `main`, so `main` has the same overlap; it is just less visible there.

Three things cause it:
- A leaving row fades out over the full 150 ms while the rows below slide up into its spot.
- An arriving row fades in from the start, while the row it replaces is still sliding out of its spot.
- A row that moves past other rows slides straight across them at full opacity. Examples: a row jumping to the top, a pin, or a row returning from an expanded Working shelf, which can travel about 800 px.

## Fix

All changes are in `Sidebar.motion.ts`, and they only use opacity and translate:
- Leaving rows are fully faded by 40% of the eased motion, before the next row's text reaches theirs.
- Arriving rows stay hidden until 60% of the eased motion, then fade in.
- A row that changes order relative to the rows around it fades out at its old spot and fades in at its new one, while the rows it passed slide one slot. "Changes order" means it is not part of the longest run of rows that kept their order. A row that would slide more th [...]

Dropping a tab on the strip's left edge makes a new column, and the panes beside it slide right to make room. While they slide, two things go wrong:

## Problem

Switching tabs or workspaces could lose a chat's place. Scroll a chat partway up, then open another tab in the same pane or switch to another workspace (keys or the overview). Come back, and the chat is at the top with "Scroll to end" showing.

title: fix(web): shrinking a column while scrolled right no longer runs away
author: flamboh
head: 4b3fe010b2ae8b43207d550dd0bb4f0369e759de
body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 on behalf of Oliver**

Fix for the redesign stack, targets layer 6 (#28845).

Stacked on #31268 and #31406; review only the commits after c64e9418b4. Retarget/merge after those land.

## Problem

With the workspace strip scrolled all the way right, dragging a column edge to shrink a column makes the strip narrower. The browser then pulls the scroll back, and the drag reads that scroll change as pointer movement. So the column runs away to its minimum width: in a 2-column strip, 240 px of pointer travel shrank the left column by 514 px, and the edge never moved on screen.

## Fix

While a column drag is in progress, the strip keeps the scrollable width it had when the drag started. A fixed-width spacer inside the scroller holds it, so the browser has no reason to pull the scroll back. The edge follows the pointer. On release the spacer goes away and the strip settles to its real width in one step.

The spacer is set once at drag start and removed once at release. Nothing changes per frame. Arrow-key resizing doesn't use the drag preview, so it is unchanged.

## Validation

Real app on a cloud dev box, headless Chrome at 1600×900, launcher-only columns, pointer moved in 4 px steps. "Gap" is drawn edge minus pointer.

2 columns, scrolled fully right, shrinking the left column:

| Step | Pointer x | Before edge | Before gap | Before scroll | After edge | After gap | After scroll |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 653 | 657 | +4 | 530 | 653 | [...]

title: fix(server): capture iOS screenshots on Xcode 26's simctl
author: shivamhwp
head: 7d1f93d83f12693ce81c025b0da5e573239de799
body:
## Problem

iOS Simulator screenshots fail on Xcode 26: the pinned device hub always passes a numeric `--display`, which Xcode 26's `simctl` rejects. Refs https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/28035

## Change

- When the hub rejects a screenshot of an iOS 26-or-older simulator, take it again with `simctl io  screenshot` on the default display.

Paragraph streaming can hide the last paragraph for as long as a provider keeps its turn open on background work. Refs https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/28175. The delegated-wake fix is separate: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/28204.

## Problem
When the first request of a Codex run hits a usage limit, Codex can emit only an empty `premium` limit notification. The failure then loses its obtainable reset time, so the recovery card cannot offer automatic continuation. Closes https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/27773.

title: fix(opencode): long command turns no longer fail when the command request times out
author: juliusmarminge
head: 63b23367b5cf6647eb3592059cac84754369c0dd
body:
## Problem

An OpenCode turn whose prompt starts with a known command (`/my-skill …`) is marked failed with "Provider turn failed." about 5 minutes after it starts, while OpenCode keeps running the command. OpenCode's `POST /session/{id}/command` does not respond until the whole command run finishes. Under Node, fetch (undici) gives up waiting for response headers after 300 s (the SDK's `req.timeout = false` only applies on Bun). The request's error handler then finalized a turn that had been admitted long before.

Reproduced on main (6575ce3250) with real `opencode serve` 1.18.18 and a project command `/slow 330` that runs `sleep 330`: the turn failed 300 s after `session.command` was sent, and OpenCode finished the command 37 s later.

## Change

In `submitPrompt` (`packages/provider-opencode/src/server/adapter.ts`), the forked `session.command` request no longer fails the turn once the command's user receipt has admitted it. From then on the event stream (`session.idle` / `session.error`) decides the outcome, the same way it already does for `promptAsync` turns. Failures before admission still fail the turn, and so does the existing 10 s admission timeout. Losing the event stream still fails the turn as before.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#27664

Triaged via the automated issue flow.

## Verification

- New test `keeps an admitted native command running when its HTTP request times out` in `packages/provider-opencode/src/server/adapter.test.ts`: on main it [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Recover request failures after command receipt completion.**

If the receipt completes and the SDK request then rejects before the admission race settles, Line 2994 skips `finalizeTurn`, but `Effect.tapError` still propagates the rejection. `Fiber.join(request)` can win `Effect.raceFirst` with that failure. The `startTurn` error handler then fails a command that OpenCode has already admitted. Recover the request failure after a completed receipt before racing the request against the receipt. Keep failures before receipt completion unchanged. ([effect.website](https://effect.website/docs/v4/error-management/error-channel-operations?utm_source=openai))

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Preserve the request failure detail for pre-admission command failures.**

When `session.command` fails before its receipt completes, `makeProviderFailure` receives the `OpenCodeRuntimeError` wrapper and no explicit message. The emitted failure is then the generic `Provider turn failed.`, even though `OpenCodeRuntimeError.detail` holds the request failure. Pass that detail as the explicit message. `makeProviderFailure` applies the existing redaction to explicit messages before it builds the failure contract.

** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Do not suppress admitted HTTP response failures.**

`Deferred.isDoneUnsafe(receipt)` proves only that OpenCode published the user receipt. OpenCode can then fail while persisting setup state. The `session.command` endpoint returns an HTTP error before runner startup and does not publish `session.error`. The current guard suppresses that rejection, so the turn can hang.

Use the nested response status to distinguish a definite OpenCode response failure from a transport failure. Keep suppression for admitted errors without an HTTP status, including `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`.

This repeats the native-command admission setup immediately above. Could you fold the timeout and terminal assertion into that existing test instead?

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Scope the argument checks to the intended objects.**

These regexes search the complete expression instead of the actual argument structure. title: fix(server): Antigravity install no longer fails on a stale Windows Crashpad pipe
author: juliusmarminge
head: 7c78ead442f19a9efb5068f13ffb80f0a7e2e892
body:
## Problem

On Windows, installing Antigravity can fail with "Antigravity browser suppression could not be verified." This happens when the server inherits a stale `CHROME_CRASHPAD_PIPE_NAME`, for example a dead `\\.\pipe\crashpad__…` carried in through an updater or installer launch chain. The browser-preflight helper is the Electron exe run as Node, and it passed that variable through. The helper then prints a Crashpad `registration_protocol_win.cc … CreateFile` error to stderr before the marker line, so the preflight's exact stderr match fails. The install rolls back on every retry.

## Change

`CHROME_CRASHPAD_PIPE_NAME` is added to `removedEnvironmentKeys` in `apps/server/src/provider/antigravityAuthSupport.ts`. That list is matched case-insensitively and feeds `antigravityEnvironment`, which builds the environment for the browser preflight, for the ACP runtime, and for the sign-in `BROWSER` helper the runtime starts. None of these children need a Crashpad pipe, and T3 registers no crash reporter of its own. The strict stderr check is unchanged.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#26368

Triaged via the automated issue flow.

## Verification

- `vp test run apps/server/src/provider/antigravityAuthSupport.test.ts`: the existing test "Antigravity process environment > isolates the profile and harness after merging overrides without changing the base environment" now puts `CHROME_CRASHPAD_PIPE_NAME` and a lowercase alias in its base env.

title: fix(desktop): agents see visible:true while the desktop shows their tab
author: shivamhwp
head: 00af236c3f9a5e65474e49c3bd9dd3dcac355634
body:
## Problem

Agents saw a preview tab as `visible: false` while the desktop app's Browser panel was showing it, and could be handed a different, hidden tab when they called the preview tools without a `tabId`. Refs https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/17015

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Wait for desktop tab acquisition before reporting `shown: true`.**

The queue retains pre-acquisition operations, but it runs the first operation before `createTab`. `PreviewManager.setShown` ignores the call when the tab is not yet registered. Because `clientSettingsHydrated` is not a dependency, the effect does not retry after acquisition.

replies.body: Already fixed in 70ee122: the effect now returns early until `clientSettingsHydrated` and lists it in the dependencies, so the report runs after `acquireDesktopTab` has queued `createTab`.

title: fix(server): price Antigravity Gemini Flash effort variants
author: Ephraim-9
head: 765670cbf47ca72357148c6bd28bc9a6db7692fb
body:
## Problem

On Usage, most Antigravity tokens show as **Unpriced**. Two causes:

- The reader's `MODEL_IDS` table stopped at Gemini 3.1 Pro / 3 Flash, so current Gemini Flash generations fell through to labels like `antigravity-model-1319` ([#19189](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/19189)).
- Name-based records carry Antigravity's effort and routing suffixes (`-low`, `-medium`, `-high`, `-extra-low`, `-tiered`, `-control`, `-thinking`, `-agent`), which the LiteLLM rate table does not list.

## Change

`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/antigravityUsageReader.ts`:

- Adds the current Gemini Flash ids (1020, 1072, 1073, 1132, 1133, 1187, 1298, 1299, 1301, 1318, 1319, 1320, 1322) and 342 to `MODEL_IDS`, using the names Antigravity writes in conversation metadata.
- Sets `rateModel` on every emitted Antigravity record to the base model with the variant suffix stripped, the same mechanism Cursor uses through `cursorRateModel`. `gemini-3.8-flash-high` keeps its display name and prices as `gemini-3.8-flash`; `gemini-3-flash-*` prices as `gemini-3-flash-preview`, the only name the table has (matching existing ids 1018/1047/1084).
- `rateModel` is derived once, in the emission loop, after alias merging has settled the final model. A model-less step that adopts a named generation's model through merging is priced too.

Known limits: id 342 (`gpt-oss-120b-medium`) gains a readable name but stays unpriced, because LiteLLM has no bare `gpt-oss-120b` and its provider-prefixed entr [...]

🟡 **Medium** `usage/antigravityUsageReader.ts:263`

Alias de-duplication can leave a merged record displaying a known `model` while retaining `rateModel: "antigravity-unknown"`, so pricing still treats that usage as unpriced. `rateModel` is computed here before `merge` can replace an unknown model with the other alias's known model; recompute it whenever `merge` changes `model`.

No longer relevant as of fdcbdd1b2d18748027bc44e20f5d7e4640d9e4e8

replies.body: Fixed in 33bfddf949: `merge` now picks the model first and recomputes `rateModel` from it. Added a regression test (`prices a merged Antigravity alias by the model it adopts`) where a model-less step merges with a named generation; it received `antigravity-unknown` before the change and `gemini-3.8-flash` after.
